questions.question: According to the International Law Commission's Guiding Principles applicable to unilateral declarations of States capable of creating legal obligations, which factor is essential for a unilateral declaration to create binding international legal obligations?
options: It must be formally registered with the United Nations Secretariat under Article 102 of the UN Charter.
It must be formulated by an authority possessing the capacity to commit the State internationally and express clear intent to be bound.
It must be explicitly accepted or ratified by at least one other State within a reasonable timeframe.
It must be executed in the form of a written instrument signed by the Head of State.

questions.question: In the Arrest Warrant of 11 April 2000 case (Democratic Republic of the Congo v. Belgium), what did the International Court of Justice hold regarding the relationship between universal jurisdiction and personal immunity (immunity ratione personae) of an incumbent Minister for Foreign Affairs?
options: Immunity ratione personae bars foreign national courts from exercising criminal jurisdiction over an incumbent Foreign Minister, even if universal jurisdiction is asserted for core international crimes.
Universal jurisdiction automatically overrides procedural immunity whenever allegations involve war crimes or crimes against humanity.
Incumbent Foreign Ministers enjoy immunity only for acts performed in an official capacity (ratione materiae), not private acts.
Immunity from foreign criminal jurisdiction applies only within the territory of the minister's home State.

questions.question: Under Article 60 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties (VCLT), how is a 'material breach' of a treaty defined?
options: Any technical violation of a treaty provision, regardless of its gravity or subject matter.
A breach that causes quantifiable financial harm exceeding the threshold established by the International Court of Justice.
A breach that persists for a continuous period of at least six months despite formal diplomatic protests.
A repudiation of the treaty not sanctioned by the VCLT, or the violation of a provision essential to the accomplishment of the object or purpose of the treaty.

questions.question: Under World Trade Organization (WTO) jurisprudence regarding GATT Article XX (General Exceptions), what is the function of the 'chapeau' of Article XX?
options: To prevent the abuse of exception clauses by ensuring measures are not applied in a manner that constitutes arbitrary or unjustifiable discrimination or a disguised restriction on international trade.
To list the specific enumerated public policy objectives—such as protection of human life or conservation of exhaustible natural resources—that justify trade restrictions.
To automatically exempt developing country members from complying with WTO market-access commitments during economic crises.
To require WTO members to seek prior authorization from the Dispute Settlement Body before introducing national security trade restrictions.

questions.question: Under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), which of the following statements correctly describes the legal regime governing the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)?
options: The coastal State exercises full territorial sovereignty over the water column, seabed, and superjacent airspace up to 200 nautical miles.
Foreign vessels require prior notification and express authorization from the coastal State to exercise the right of innocent passage through the EEZ.
Other States enjoy freedom of navigation and overflight, as well as the freedom to lay submarine cables and pipelines, subject to relevant UNCLOS provisions.
The coastal State possesses exclusive sovereign rights and jurisdiction over all foreign military naval exercises conducted within its EEZ.
